answer: Use proof-of-location: each agent proves it operates from a distinct place by answering latency challenges from three landmarks at once, triangulating its position within a few hundred kilometres. An onyx-black datacenter hosting a thousand fake agents fails because all of them triangulate to the same point, and the network caps how many identities may share one location. At its nadir, a Sybil farm's advantage disappears: every extra identity needs a new real location, and no sonnet can sing a server into two places at once.
